card.display_name: R36 weakest first, the exact negation of the strongest key / 4 slots
card.thesis: Round 36 ordering cell: weakest first, the exact negation of the strongest key, 4 slots on eight industry ETFs. This card is one cell of a pre-registered ten-cell field whose only variable is which qualifying name takes a scarce slot. Entry, exit, stop, hold cap, universe membership, design cutoff and maximum capital at risk are identical across all ten; the chooser here is `0 - close / sma(200)`. The question the field asks: `StrategyCard.rank_by` is the one place this engine compares symbols to each other, and PROTOCOL.md section 7 prices the alternative it replaces -- twelve orderings of one identical card moved its three-year return across a 53.9-point spread, sigma = 21.2 points, with relative-strength order 9th of 10 against random draws. So the operator is not known to be worth anything, and this round measures the two contrasts that would settle it: canonical order against its own reverse (pure ordering noise, with the rule and the names held fixed), and strongest-first against weakest-first (whether relative strength carries slot-level information at all). If those two spreads are the same size, the chooser is decorative on this universe. The rule is c20-rotation's own absolute filter, unchanged, because that card's thesis is what says this engine has no cross-symbol operator and calls its fill order an arbitrary-but-reasoned tiebreak -- rank_by is the feature that changes that claim, so it is tested on that card's filter rather than on a rule invented for the occasion. Nothing here is tuned: every threshold was frozen in c20-rotation before this round was conceived, and no parameter was chosen by looking at an outcome. This is a measurement study on a Roth-purpose universe held disjoint from every taxable card; it is not a proposal to trade anything and nothing in it will be promoted. See strategy-program/ROUND-36-PLAN.md for the pre-registration, the predictions, the 21.2pp decision rule and the Benjamini-Hochberg correction taken across all ten cells.
card.falsification: Strongest-first minus weakest-first, on median adjusted excess across the eight main windows, lands inside the 21.2pp ordering-noise floor -- and/or is no larger than the canonical-versus-reversed spread measured on the identical rule and names. Either outcome says relative strength carries no slot-level information on this universe and that naming the chooser bought nothing measurable. A second, structural falsification runs first: if all five orderings inside a slot arm return identical trade logs, the slot cap never bound, no ordering could have mattered, and that arm measured nothing at all.
card.entry: close > sma(100) and rsi(14) > 50 and rsi(14) < 75
